desc: Parse input: N, sorted array A, Q queries (L, R).
Compute nxt[i] for each i: smallest index j (1-based) with A[j] >= 2*A[i], via bisect on A; M[i] = nxt[i] - i (treat missing as infinity).
Build a sparse table for range maximum queries over M.
For each query [L,R] with len = R-L+1, binary search the largest K in [0, len//2] such that rangeMax(L, L+K-1) <= len - K.
Implement the complete solution in Python with fast I/O (sys.stdin.buffer).
Verify the greedy/feasibility logic against both provided samples (all Sample 1 answers and Sample 2 spot-checks match).
Check sparse table construction loop bounds and range_max indexing for off-by-one errors (audited: bisect bounds, st row ranges, log2 table, binary search all correct).
